quote: was adopted by the AU Executive Council during its 45th Ordinary Session
reason: The AU Executive Council adopted the Strategy, but the document does not say it creates any law or regulation with legal force.

quote: Develop a 5 Year Implementation Plan of the Continental AI Strategy
reason: Under the heading 'The African Union Commission to:', the AUC gets specific duties (implementation plan, risk research, annual safety conference, expert group), though most action areas have no single owner.

quote: Mobilise regional and international development funds, with private and philanthropic funding,
reason: Funding sources are named for a proposed regional fund, but no amount or budget is stated anywhere.

quote: Organise two forums on “Financing Responsible AI for Africa ”, between 2025 and 2030.
reason: This is a numerical target with a deadline, though it is only an output count; the document has no numerical outcome targets.
resolution_note: A number with a deadline meets level 2 as written. It is the AU's only numeric target and it counts forums, not outcomes.

quote: including the provision of upskilling and reskilling programmes and requirements for jobs at risk
reason: Beyond skills goals, it commits to reskilling for jobs at risk (p.7) and to national policy on labour transformations (p.51).

quote: Establish a regional independent AI Ethics Board, which reviews applications from AI research groups
reason: It names specific mechanisms: an ethics review board for large-scale systems, red-teaming, transparency registers and impact assessments.

quote: data transfers for AI in line with the Malabo Convention and AU Data Policy Framework
reason: It links AI data transfers to the Malabo Convention, which page 26 names as the AU Convention on Cybersecurity and Personal Data Protection.

quote: enforce compliance with standards as they emerge, and provide access to redress and remedy
reason: Enforcement bodies and redress are only proposed for the future with no penalties or process stated, so this is scored at the lower level.

quote: promote investment in natural language processing capabilities in local and indigenous African languages
reason: Local-language AI is a stated goal, but no specific dataset, model or fund is named, so this is scored at the lower level.

quote: Conducting a midterm review of the continental AI strategy in 2027 to refine indicators
reason: It sets a 2027 review date and an M&E portal, but the readiness-index indicators are not yet named and no reviewer is designated, so this is scored at the lower level.

quote: Egypt is adopting its second edition of the National AI Strategy
reason: The document calls itself a strategy, and the only adoption language credits 'Egypt' plus a presidential launch (p2) without naming an approving cabinet, parliament or equivalent body, so between 0 and 1 the lower score applies; the AI law is described only as in development (p10).

quote: formalize, approve and govern the implementation of Egypt’s National AI Strategy
reason: The National Council for Artificial Intelligence is named with a stated duty to govern implementation, though most initiatives name no owner.
resolution_note: The National Council for AI is named with the stated duty to govern implementation, which meets level 2.

quote: Create national AI fund equivalent of $430-860M
reason: An amount range is given, but no committed source is stated (only a benchmark of 0.1%-0.15% of GDP), and the startup fund on p40 names possible contributors but no amount, so between 1 and 2 the lower score applies.

quote: The number of AI professionals/experts is expected to double to 30,000 by 2030.
reason: Numerical targets with deadlines are stated, such as 30,000 AI experts by 2030 and the 7.7% GDP contribution by 2030.

quote: we will continue to prioritize investments in skill development and capacity building
reason: Skills and training goals are extensive, and the negative impact of AI on employment is listed as a threat (p12), but no transition, retraining or social protection plan for displaced workers is given.

quote: protecting all citizens against high-risk or prohibited AI
reason: The document commits to high-risk and prohibited AI categories in the planned AI law and to guidelines for classifying AI system risks under the Center for Responsible AI.

quote: The Egyptian Data Protection Law (No. 151 of 2020)
reason: The named Data Protection Law is linked to AI governance, and a Personal Data Protection Authority is named (p19).

quote: While the Egyptian AI law is currently in its final development phase
reason: AI rules, bylaws and a regulatory body are to be developed later (p25); the only stated penalties belong to the data protection authority (p19) and existing cybercrime law, not to AI-specific rules, so between 1 and 2 the lower score applies.
resolution_note: The AI law is still being drafted (p10). The penalties rater B cited belong to the data protection law, which is scored under data protection.

quote: Fine-tuning Large Language Models for Arabic language use for specific sectors.
reason: Concrete commitments are made to Arabic models and to sectoral Arabic datasets (Initiative 7, p31, with 'Data sets' as a deliverable).

quote: National AI capacity will be evaluated at least annually through periodic assessments.
reason: The document has named indicators (CAF, 89 indicators) and a schedule (annual review, 1/3/5-year milestones) but names no reviewer, so all three elements for a 2 are not met and the lower score applies.

quote: The strategy provides a comprehensive framework to guide Kenya
reason: The document calls itself a strategy and framework, says on page 40 that Kenya has no AI law, and records only stakeholder validation workshops (p.23) and a ministerial foreword, with no stated adoption by cabinet or parliament.

quote: Government institutions will provide regulatory and policy guidance, private-sector actors will drive innovation
reason: Responsibility is spread loosely across sectors; the Ministry is named as author (p.40, p.89), but no flagship project in Tables 5.2–5.8 is assigned to a named implementing body.

quote: national AI and emerging tech innovation fund (from the R&D 2% of GDP
reason: A source is named (the National Research Fund's R&D allocation), but no amount is set for the AI fund itself; the 2% of GDP is the overall R&D figure, so the lower score applies.

quote: Build three TIA 942 (ANSI standard) AI-capable data centres within 5 years
reason: This is a numerical target with a deadline; others include '2 PPP projects in the next 5 years' (p.71) and a semiconductor facility 'within five years' (p.70).

quote: Goal 4: Build a robust pipeline of competent and agile AI workers for Kenya
reason: Skills goals are detailed, but displaced workers get only a general pledge ('Potential job displacement will be proactively addressed', p.62) and a town-hall welfare suggestion (p.48), with no transition or social protection plan, so the lower score applies.

quote: Implement AI ethical and safety standards through conformity assessment schemes/safety audits
reason: Specific measures are stated: conformity assessments and safety audits, a planned national AI risk and safety institute (p.78), and a mandatory ethical impact assessment for the public sector (p.81).

quote: existing laws such as the Data Protection Act and the Consumer Protection Act
reason: The document names the Data Protection Act as a foundational framework for AI issues, and lists the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner as a key regulatory stakeholder (p.50).

quote: As AI matures in Kenya, develop an AI and Other Emerging Technologies Act and regulations
reason: Legislation is deferred to the future and a complaints mechanism is only to be developed (p.81); no penalties, sanctions or enforcement process are stated.

quote: a maternal health chatbot in local dialects to provide accurate pregnancy
reason: Local-language use cases are only 'under consideration', with no dedicated datasets, models or funding committed; the $1 billion Microsoft/G42 initiative on p.54 is described as existing partner investment, not a strategy commitment, so the lower score applies.

quote: creating a monitoring and evaluation framework to track progress
reason: The tables list KPIs, but no reviewer or review schedule is named and the M&E framework is only promised, so the lower score applies.

quote: This National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (NAIS) is a living document
reason: The document calls itself a strategy and 'living document'; it states no cabinet, parliamentary or equivalent approval and creates no law.

quote: A well-functioning and respected AI Governance Regulatory System promoted by NITDA
reason: NITDA is named, and an AI Governance Regulatory Body is proposed, but no body has stated duties for implementing the whole strategy, and implementation is described as a loose multi-stakeholder effort (p.5), so the lower level applies.

quote: Secure additional funding from the public and private sectors.
reason: Funding is mentioned, including a proposed AI R&D Fund (p.41) and public/private sources, but no amount is committed for the strategy; the US$20 million figure (p.15) describes an existing donor programme.

quote: Nigeria aims to reduce unemployment by five percentage points by equipping at least 70%
reason: There are numerical targets without specific deadlines (also the <50% grid target, p.32) and deadlines without numbers ('within five years', p.34); the 3MTT four-year figure (p.47) describes a pre-existing programme, not a target of this strategy, so the lower level applies.

quote: Examples include protecting workers' rights through retraining programmes, tailored unemployment benefits
reason: Skills goals (p.35, p.41) are paired with a job-displacement horizon scan and legislative reforms covering retraining and unemployment benefits for affected workers.

quote: provide a structured approach for evaluating the ethical implications of AI projects before deployment
reason: The document commits to specific risk measures: a pre-deployment AI ethics assessment framework and a National AI Risk Management Framework with protocols for assessing safety risks (p.47).

quote: adherence to the Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023
reason: A named data protection law, the NDPA 2023, is explicitly linked to the strategy's data protection principle and discussed at length (pp.19-20).
resolution_note: Both raters gave 2. Rater B cited p28; the quote is on p29.

quote: ensure compliance with ethical standards, and mediate potential disputes
reason: A future regulatory body would ensure compliance and adjudicate, and legislative reforms are planned (p.45), but no penalties, sanctions or concrete enforcement process are stated, so the lower level applies.

quote: Replicating Nigeria’s social context and cultural diversity with AI tools and solutions
reason: Local context and cultural diversity are stated as goals, but local languages are never mentioned and no datasets, models or funding are named for them.

quote: outlining timelines, key performance indicators (KPIs) for progress tracking
reason: KPIs and a 'Monitor & Review' risk step updated 'periodically' (p.53) are referenced, but no indicators, named reviewer or review schedule are actually set out in the document.

quote: The National Artificial Intelligence Policy for the Republic of Rwanda serves as a roadmap
reason: The document calls itself a roadmap and policy, and it states no adoption by cabinet, parliament or another approving body; the only attribution is 'MINICT - 2022'.

quote: The RAI Office is to be given the mandate to implement the National AI Policy
reason: The Responsible AI Office within MINICT is named with stated duties (coordinating implementation, monitoring and evaluation, communications), and each implementation-plan activity names a lead institution, although the office is proposed for establishment in year one rather than already existing.

quote: support the financing by building upon the Seed Investment Fund to co-invest alongside specialist funds
reason: Funding sources are mentioned (Seed Investment Fund, public-sector funding, risk-sharing and co-investment funds), but no amount appears anywhere; page 9 says the full plan includes a budget, but this summary shows none.

quote: Set Up a taskforce to research and identify a portfolio of 5 National AI Projects
reason: There are some numbers (5 National AI Projects) and some deadlines (RAI Office in the first year), but no number is tied to a stated deadline; the FY column headers show no readable timing per activity, and all indicators are 'Number of...' with no target values, so the lower score applies.

quote: Commit to reskilling the workforce with 21st Century AI and data skills.
reason: Skills, upskilling and reskilling goals are extensive, but there are no plans for workers displaced by AI and no transition support or social protection; general employee reskilling is borderline, so the lower score applies.

quote: Initiate regulatory sandbox projects on Al to provide controlled testing environment
reason: Beyond general risk and ethics language, the document commits to regulatory sandbox projects that provide a controlled testing environment to evaluate AI solutions against the ethics guidelines, which is a specific testing measure.
resolution_note: Regulatory sandboxes giving a controlled environment to test and evaluate AI solutions (p21) are a testing measure named at level 2.

quote: cloud service providers under the supervisory authority (NCSA) as required by law (DPP)
reason: The implementation plan links to a named data protection law (DPP) and names the supervisory authority (NCSA), including an activity to 'Enforce the Data Protection & Privacy law'.

quote: By strengthening the capacity of regulatory authorities to understand and regulate AI
reason: AI regulation is framed as future capacity-building and future sector-specific guidelines, with no AI penalties or sanctions; the compliance audits on page 14 apply only to cloud providers under existing law, so between 1 and 2 the lower score applies.

I looked for mentions of Kinyarwanda, other local languages, local-language datasets or models, and adapting AI to local cultural context, and found none; references to 'local' concern solution providers and data value-chains, not language or context.
resolution_note: No language is mentioned. 'Tailored guidelines' are ethics guidelines, not a commitment to local language or context.

quote: the RAI Office or RAIO will be tasked with the monitor-ing and evaluation
reason: A reviewer (RAIO) and output indicators are named, but no schedule for reviewing the policy is given; the annual AI Readiness Index is a benchmark rather than a policy review, so the lower score applies.
